To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) AP‐1 DNA‐binding activity was diminished in lymphocytes isolated from old (> 12 months) mice and activated with Con A.
the expression of the c‐fos protooncogene and formation of the transcription factor AP‐ 1 are decreased during aging of the lymphoid system in vivo.
the expression of c‐FoS and the AP‐1 transcription factor are decreased in Con A stimulated lymphocytes derived from aged mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of c‐fos in cellular senescence of lymphocytes.
the role of AP‐1 transcription factor in cellular senescence.
the loss of AP‐1 transcriptional activity as a possible mechanism of cell cycle arrest in aging lymphocytes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the loss of AP‐1 activity in lymphocytes from old mice is a consequence of the diminished c‐fos expression and not a result of the impaired function of c‐Jun protein.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AP‐1 DNA‐binding activity in ConA‐stimulated lymphocytes from old mice is decreased due to a decrease in Fos expression.
c‐Fos protein expression and AP‐1 formation is impaired in Con A stimulated lymphocytes from old mice and this is a feature of cellular senesence in lymphocytes in vivo.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the loss of AP‐1 DNA‐binding activity in lymphocytes from old mice is a feature of cellular senesce.
the transcriptional activity of AP‐1 is diminished in aged lymphocytes, which is likely to be responsible for the decreased expression of protooncogenes, such as c‐fos.
